subject: English
central_question: How can a student convert mixed direct speech into consistent reported speech while preserving sentence type, meaning, pronouns, tense, and modal force?
in_scope_units: Mixed-dialogue conversion across speakers and sentence types
Reporting questions that also function as polite requests
Reporting conditional sentences with consistent backshift
Reporting modals of deduction without unnecessary change
banned_topics: Active and passive voice rules unrelated to reporting

known_pitfalls.claim: Each sentence in a reported passage can use a different tense pattern without regard to the reporting verb.
known_pitfalls.correction: Once a past reporting frame is established, tense and pronoun changes must remain consistent throughout the passage unless meaning clearly requires otherwise.

known_pitfalls.claim: A command is reported like an ordinary statement.
known_pitfalls.correction: An imperative is normally reported with an appropriate reporting verb followed by object + to-infinitive or not to-infinitive.

known_pitfalls.claim: Every must changes to had to in reported speech.
known_pitfalls.correction: Must expressing pure deduction usually remains must; only must expressing obligation normally changes to had to.

recommended_example_progression: Convert a statement and request from a short dialogue
Report a polite question-request using asked to or asked if
Backshift both clauses of a conditional sentence
Keep must unchanged when it expresses deduction
Convert a mixed passage containing a statement, command, and exclamation
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: Typical CBSE practice presents dialogue completion, mixed-sentence reporting, paragraph conversion, and error correction.
